findings.title: firestore.rules deny blocks are redundant with the existing default-deny
findings.problem: The three new explicit `allow read, write: if false;` matches for trainers/referralCodes/trainerLinks are redundant with the existing trailing `match /{document=**} { allow read, write: if false; }` catch-all. Not wrong, but the design implies they are functionally required.
findings.fix: Add a note in §4 that the three matches are deliberately explicit/self-documenting guards, redundant with the default-deny; removing them changes nothing functionally.

findings.title: Signed-URL ADC-without-key caution does not match this repo's firebase.ts
findings.problem: firebase.ts has no Application Default Credentials path: both branches use admin.credential.cert(...) (key-bearing). The warning that getSignedUrl throws under keyless ADC is harmless but over-stated for this codebase.
findings.fix: Reword §2.3 to note the current config always uses key-bearing cert credentials so signing works everywhere configured; keep the url:null fallback and no-real-signed-URL-in-emulator rule only as defense for a future ADC/emulator setup.

findings.title: Trainer 'email if shared' references a sharing flag that is not modeled
findings.problem: GET /api/student/trainer returns the trainer's 'email if shared', but the trainers doc defines a plain email with no visibility flag, and the only sharing toggle is shareProgressWithTrainer (photos). The 'if shared' qualifier has no backing mechanism.
findings.fix: Pick one: (a) drop 'if shared' and always return trainer contact email (trainer contact is not private student data), or (b) add trainers/{trainerId}.contactEmailPublic:boolean (default true) and gate on it. (a) is simpler and matches requirement 7.

findings.title: Register->link provider write should be pinned to a non-disposed Ref
findings.problem: linkTrainer is awaited after register(), but the auth-state redirect can dispose the register screen while the call is in flight. The provider-write approach survives this only if the write goes through a Ref/notifier that outlives the widget, not a disposed WidgetRef.
findings.fix: State explicitly in §6.4 that linkTrainer writes linkTrainerResultProvider via a provider container/notifier (captured before navigation), not via a WidgetRef that may be disposed, so a mid-flight teardown cannot drop the result.
